brief: A seven-cell honeycomb standing on at least three stud spikes facing down as feet.

requirements.evidence: Seven full hex bases (piece:0,0,0 centre plus the six ring cells at q/r offsets (-1,0), (-1,1), (0,-1), (0,1), (1,-1), (1,0)) on level 0, forming a flower. Caps close the open faces and joint bolts lock the joints.

requirements.requirement: Standing on at least three stud spikes
requirements.evidence: Three stud spikes (spike:0#-1,0|-1,1|0,0, spike:0#0,-1|0,0|1,-1, spike:0#0,0|0,1|1,0) placed at evenly spaced outer junctions on the underside of level 0. check_build reports no issues and meshClash clear.
Spikes were added with facing 'down' and variant 'stud' and the configurator accepted them. I could not view the underside in the render to confirm visually, so this rests on the accepted op.

finish.summary: Built a seven-cell hex flower on one level (centre plus six surrounding full bases), capped the open faces, locked the joints, and added three stud spikes facing down at evenly spaced outer junctions as feet. check_build is clean with meshClash clear. No props were added since the brief concerns structure only.

lines.label: M6 brass heat-set insert, 7.6 mm (initeq M6-1.0 Short)
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
